# Vendor risk areas: what to ask for

Ask for more evidence as criticality and data access rise.

| Area | Low-risk vendor | Critical vendor or personal data access |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Financial | Basic company information | Recent financial signals, customer concentration, length in business |
| Security | Security contact and basic practices | Independent certification with scope and date, questionnaire, penetration test summary, access controls, encryption |
| Privacy | Confirm no personal data | Data processing agreement, data location, subprocessors list, retention and deletion, breach notification time |
| Compliance | Applicable rules confirmed | Evidence for each rule in the company's jurisdictions; sanctions check |
| Continuity | Support hours | Continuity and recovery plans, tested recovery times, exit and data return plan |
| Contract | Standard terms | Liability, indemnity, termination, auto-renewal, price change and audit rights reviewed by legal |
| Conduct | Conflict of interest declaration | Declarations from staff involved in the selection |

Least privilege: a vendor should receive only the data and access the service needs, for only as long as it needs them. A request for "all customer data" to deliver a narrow service is a high finding.
